extracted.intended_audience: consumers of health news, journalists, public relations/health communicators, and others interested in the quality of health-care information
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance about what HealthNewsReview.org looks for when evaluating health care journalism and related messages — emphasizing accuracy, balance, completeness, disclosure of tradeoffs, and empowering consumers for shared decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: improve public dialogue and promote shared decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of HealthNewsReview.org is to improve the public dialogue about health care by helping consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions and by promoting the principles of shared decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviews and criteria to foster better public conversation about health care and to support decisions informed by accurate, balanced, and complete information about tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate, balanced and complete information about tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Content should provide 'accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a story communicates benefits and harms, limitations, uncertainties, and comparative tradeoffs clearly and without distortion; this is central to supporting shared decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Helping consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide consumers with criteria and explanations they can use to judge the strength of claims (e.g., evidence quality, magnitude of benefit, conflicts of interest). The site explicitly aims to teach this skill rather than only to judge content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate across message types that influence consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org 'evaluates health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rubric applies not just to news stories but to promotional and PR materials as well; assess intent, framing, and potential to mislead across those formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Star score (0–5) as review rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Searchable review rating: 'Type 0 - 5 star to search by review rating. ie. 3 star or 1 star.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site uses a 0–5 star summary rating for reviews (detail on how the star score is determined is provided on a linked page). Star ratings are a concise summary of the review evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about funding and editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that prior funding 'never had any influence over the editorial operation of the project' and disclosure that previous support has ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and disclose editorial independence and funding sources; transparency about funders and editorial control is an implicit standard of credibility for the review project itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide consumers tools and criteria to evaluate messages themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: The site 'provides criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond individual reviews, offer toolkits, tips for understanding studies, and links to other resources so readers can apply the evaluation criteria independently.
